newsitem.title: USA: Apple paid $430 million for Next Software.
newsitem.headline: Apple paid $430 million for Next Software.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. said Monday it paid $430 million to buy Next Software Inc. -- $30 million higher than previously estimated, and that it expected a substantial loss in its fiscal second quarter because of the deal.

Apple also revealed in documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission that it did not expect to report a profit until at least its fiscal fourth quarter ending in September, if not later.
It was the first warning by the Cupertino, Calif.-based company that it might not return to profits this fiscal year, contrary to what Apple executives had said in recent weeks.

In the documents, the company revealed detailed terms of the Next acquisition, which was announced in December and completed last week. Apple bought Next to jump start an effort to revamp the fundamental software of the Macintosh computer.

Apple paid $325 million in cash, issued 1.5 million shares and assumed about $55 million of Next's debts. With about $5 million in closing costs, the price came out to $430 million, the company said. Apple had previously put the price at $400 million.
About 75 percent of the price will be expensed in the second quarter ending in March, Apple said. The company did not estimate how big its loss will be for the quarter.
In the quarter ended in December, Apple reported a $120 million loss because of weak Macintosh sales.
Since then, Apple has outlined a restructuring plan -- the second in 12 months -- that will involve layoffs to return the company to profits.
